tool.name: OGSTools shp2msh
tool.description: Mesh a shapefile and convert it to VTU
tool.command: ## A shapefile is a set of files, the index may be missing. export SHAPE_RESTORE_SHX=YES && ## Galaxy keeps the components of a shapefile dataset under fixed names in ## the dataset's extra files directory; the dataset itself is just an index ## file that GDAL cannot read. shapefile='$input_shp.extra_files_path/shapefile.shp' && if [ ! -e "\$shapefile" ]; then echo "The input dataset contains no shapefile.shp component." >&2; exit 1; fi && shp2msh --input "\$shapefile" --output output.vtu #if str($cellsize) != "" --cellsize $cellsize #end if $meshing $simplify

param.name: cellsize
param.label: Cell size
param.help: Cell size of the mesh. It is also used by the simplification: points closer than half the cell size are removed. Leave empty to use 1/100 of the larger bounding box extent.

param.name: simplify
param.label: Geometry simplification
param.help: Simplify the shapefile with the Douglas-Peucker algorithm before meshing.

tool.help:
**Overview**
`shp2msh` creates a two-dimensional mesh from the polygons of a shapefile. The shapefile is read with geopandas, overlapping polygons are merged, and the resulting geometry is meshed with either [Triangle](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake/triangle.html) or [Gmsh](https://gmsh.info/). The mesh is written as a VTU file.
**Inputs**
- **Input shapefile**: the shapefile to mesh. Its accompanying files (`.shx`, `.dbf`) are used when present; a missing index file is rebuilt. - **Cell size**: target cell size of the mesh. It is also used for the optional simplification, which removes points that are closer to each other than half the cell size. If left empty, 1/100 of the larger bounding box extent is used. - **Meshing algorithm**: Triangle or Gmsh. - **Geometry simplification**: keep the polygons unchanged (original) or simplify them with the Douglas-Peucker algorithm before meshing.
**Outputs**
The generated mesh as a VTU file with triangular cells.
